key_insight: Hybrid QM/ML calculations reveal how partial dislocations and fault ribbons stabilise ⟨a⟩ loop cores in α-Zr, with Fe and H favouring faulted segments and Sn and Nb favouring perfect segments.
engineering_relevance: These mechanisms can inform models of solute trapping and irradiation-induced microstructure evolution in zirconium nuclear fuel cladding.
method: Hybrid quantum mechanics/machine learning modelling of prismatic ⟨a⟩ loops.
Characterisation of nine dislocation line segments across three loop variants.
QM/ML nudged elastic band calculations of glide barriers and faulted-to-perfect transitions.
evidence_signal: Across nine characterised line segments, calculations identify solute-binding preferences and solute-driven partial motion, recombination and local unfaulting.
watch_item: The abstract reports atomistic mechanisms but provides no quantitative uncertainty or validation against reactor-scale behaviour.
paper_title: Comprehensive QM/ML Study of Dislocation Loop Line Segments in α-Zr Part I: <a> Loop Core Geometries, Solute Binding, and Transition Barriers
